hook.text: A superheater tube in a power plant swells and thins over years — creep and corrosion attack simultaneously.

buildup.text: At high temperature, creep deformation cracks the oxide scale — exposing fresh metal to accelerated oxidation.

discovery.text: Oxidation thins the load-bearing wall — increasing stress — which accelerates creep in a vicious feedback loop.

twist.text: Neither creep nor corrosion alone would cause failure in the expected lifetime — together they halve it.

climax.text: Power plant boiler tubes are designed with combined creep-corrosion allowances — learned from decades of failures.

punchline.text: When time, temperature, and chemistry attack together, the clock ticks faster.

quiz.question: How do creep and corrosion interact at high temperature?
options: Creep cracks the oxide and corrosion thins the wall, accelerating both
